N34a.text: Lyrics drafted by Claude, an AI model made by Anthropic, PBC. Anthropic filed to go public on October 26, 2026. Its filing reports a first-half 2026 net loss of $80.7 billion, of which $72.4 billion is a non-cash charge on its convertible notes and SAFEs that grew with its valuation. Reuters, citing a draft of the filing, reported $518 billion in committed future infrastructure spending. This is satire, not investment advice.
N34a.m6: revised after the M6 audits (log/audits/2026-10-31_m6_*.md, log/decisions.md 6)

N34r1.text: “Who needs a dollar when the bank’ll float a loan?” Today the borrowing is mostly bonds, not margin: about $500 billion of AI-related debt was issued in 2026 by October, some $200 billion of it by Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle, and at least 18 data center deals priced at double-digit yields.
N34r1.source: Bloomberg via Crypto Briefing (Oct 10, 2026) and CRE Daily (Oct 28, 2026)
N34r1.note: lyric references (human request 2026-11-01): the specific facts behind lines of the lyrics; company names only in the credits (brief)

N34r2.text: “A holdin’ company holds ’em”: Samuel Insull’s 1920s utility empire was a pyramid of leveraged holding companies owning one another’s shares, and it collapsed in 1932. Today the money circles: Nvidia has invested $30 billion in OpenAI and up to $10 billion in Anthropic, which both run on its chips, and guaranteed up to $105 billion for an OpenAI data center.
N34r2.source: EBSCO Research Starters (Insull); The Conversation via Phys.org (Oct 18, 2026); Data Center Knowledge (Aug 19, 2026)
N34r2.note: lyric references (human request 2026-11-01): the specific facts behind lines of the lyrics; company names only in the credits (brief)

N34r3.text: “The fella with the cloud boom” is Alphabet. On October 28, Google Cloud revenue was up 103% to $30.7 billion, but free cash flow was negative $9.1 billion after $51.4 billion of capital spending. Its shares fell almost 13% the next day.
N34r3.source: Alphabet Q3 2026 earnings release (8-K, Oct 28, 2026); Fortune (Oct 30, 2026)
N34r3.note: lyric references (human request 2026-11-01): the specific facts behind lines of the lyrics; company names only in the credits (brief)

N34b.text: Where 1929 doesn't fit: by 1932 the Dow was down about 89% from its peak, and it took until 1954 to regain that peak. This week was two bad days, so far.
N34b.m6: revised after the M6 audits (log/audits/2026-10-31_m6_*.md, log/decisions.md 6)

N34c.text: In 1929, buyers put about 10% down; today's US rules (Regulation T) require 50% up front for most stock bought on margin. And much of today's AI spending comes from large, profitable companies, not small investors on credit.
N34c.source: song doc, 'Where 1929 doesn't fit' (Leverage, Who's spending)
